question: During the period 268–232 BCE, who among the following was the first ruler who inscribed his messages to his subjects and officials on stone surfaces — natural rocks as well as polished pillars?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ashoka was the first ruler to inscribe his messages to his subjects on stone surfaces during his reign from 268 to 232 BCE.
 
• His inscriptions were carved on natural rocks and polished pillars across the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The messages inscribed were primarily edicts promoting Buddhism and moral teachings, known as the "Edicts of Ashoka".
 
• These inscriptions were written in various scripts, including Brahmi, Kharosthi, and Greek, reaching a wide audience.
 
• Ashoka's inscriptions are considered one of the earliest written records in Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Edicts of Ashoka:**

 
 
• These are a collection of more than 30 inscriptions on pillars, boulders, and cave walls made by Emperor Ashoka.
 
• The edicts are significant as they provide insights into Ashoka's efforts to spread Buddhist teachings and promote moral governance.
 
• The inscriptions emphasize non-violence, tolerance of all sects and opinions, and welfare of the people.
 
 
 
• **Brahmi Script:**
 
 
• It is one of the oldest writing systems used in South and Central Asia during Ashoka's reign.
 
• The Brahmi script was used in many of Ashoka's inscriptions and is considered the ancestor of many modern Indian scripts.
 
 
 
• **Kharosthi Script:**
 
 
• Another ancient script used in some of Ashoka's inscriptions, particularly in the northwestern regions of his empire.
 
• Unlike Brahmi, which is written from left to right, Kharosthi is written from right to left.
 
 
 
• **Spread of Buddhism:**
 
 
• Ashoka's support for Buddhism played a crucial role in its spread across Asia.
 
• He sent missionaries to various regions, including Sri Lanka, Southeast Asia, and Central Asia, to propagate Buddhist teachings.
 
 
 
• **Maurya Empire:**
 
 
• Founded by Chandragupta Maurya, the Maurya Empire was one of the largest and most powerful political and military empires in ancient India.
 
• Ashoka, the third emperor, is often credited with bringing the empire to its zenith.
